title: ビールが遮壁に

candidates.headline: 10. ビール大手、染みついた国内志向 カルテル疑惑に透けるジレンマ（日経・読売・産経・47・みんかぶ）2026/10/09
candidates.angle: Render domestic-brand beer as a literal barrier that blocks market access, so the product itself becomes exclusionary architecture reflecting the cartel-suspicion dilemma.
candidates.title: ビールが遮壁に
candidates.scene: In a supermarket aisle, oversized domestic beer cans are stacked into a continuous, high wall that separates customers on the near side from a shelf of foreign beers on the far side. A smiling brewery mascot on the near side adds another can to raise the barrier while shoppers press their hands against the wall trying to reach the blocked bottles.
candidates.reason: 国産志向が消費者の選択を守るどころか、実際には競争を遮る障壁として働いているかのような逆説をオブジェクトの逆転で示す。
candidates.visualTurn: Object inversion: the product (beer cans), normally made for consumption, is repurposed as a physical blockade preventing access to competitors.
candidates.contradiction: A product promoted as serving domestic preference is depicted physically preventing choice and competition, visually echoing the cartel-suspicion dilemma.
candidates.evidence: 10. ビール大手、染みついた国内志向 カルテル疑惑に透けるジレンマ（日経・読売・産経・47・みんかぶ）2026/10/09

evaluation.reason: A2 uses a simple, legible object inversion: cans repurposed as a physical barrier. That cleanly visualizes the paradox that ‘domestic preference’ can function as a blocker to competition, which maps closely to the headline’s suggestion of exclusion/cartel-like effects. It stays metaphorical rather than inventing a specific unreported actor or causal chain.

candidates.headline: 10. ビール大手、染みついた国内志向 カルテル疑惑に透けるジレンマ（日経・読売・産経・47・みんかぶ）2026/10/09
candidates.angle: Depict the big brewer's patriotic posture as a public performance while actual control is held by a small local retailer, making the power relationship visually inverted in light of cartel suspicions.
candidates.title: 大手が操り人形
candidates.scene: On a town-square stage a tall, polished beer-company executive in a suit poses and waves a national flag, playing the role of a public defender of local customers. Behind the stage, a modest local shopkeeper sits on an elevated throne and pulls strings attached to the executive like a marionette. A small crowd of shoppers applauds the executive onstage, unaware that the shopkeeper is directing each movement.
candidates.reason: 国産志向を掲げる大手が実は地元勢力に従属している、というジレンマを力関係の逆転で直観的に示す。
candidates.visualTurn: Role reversal: the apparent protector (the corporate executive) is revealed as a puppet controlled by the expectedly subordinate local shopkeeper.
candidates.contradiction: The company presents itself as the champion of domestic interests, but the drawing shows it actually subordinated to the local actors it claims to defend.
candidates.evidence: 10. ビール大手、染みついた国内志向 カルテル疑惑に透けるジレンマ（日経・読売・産経・47・みんかぶ）2026/10/09

evaluation.reason: A1 makes a strong, immediately readable role-reversal: the public-facing executive waves the flag while strings show a humble shopkeeper actually pulling the levers. That directly inverts the expected protector/protected relationship and ties clearly to the 'domestic-first vs cartel' dilemma. However it asserts a specific actor (local shopkeeper) actually controlling the brewer—an unreported causal claim not supported by the supplied headline.
unsupportedClaims: Implies a local shopkeeper (a named or identifiable retailer) actually controls and directs the big brewer’s actions/strategy — not stated in the headline.
Implies a single local actor is the locus of cartel control/manipulation rather than depicting a general power imbalance or coordinated industry behaviour.

candidates.headline: 10. ビール大手、染みついた国内志向 カルテル疑惑に透けるジレンマ（日経・読売・産経・47・みんかぶ）2026/10/09
candidates.angle: Show how a company's domestic-first ideology inflates a small local symbol into the locus of corporate authority, using a sudden change of scale to make that inversion visible.
candidates.title: 地元ボトルが君臨
candidates.scene: A corporate boardroom: a gigantic local beer bottle sits at the head of the long table like a chairman. Executives in suits are tiny, clustered along the table, craning their necks and taking notes as they look up anxiously at the towering bottle. One executive stands on a step stool to reach the bottle's cap as if seeking its approval.
candidates.reason: 大企業の意思決定が、実際には拡大された『地元』イメージに支配されているという本社と地域志向の矛盾をスケール変化で強調する。
candidates.visualTurn: Scale shift: a modest local bottle is blown up to occupy the position of authority at the boardroom table, making the local-first instinct visually rule the big firm.
candidates.contradiction: Although the firm is large and expected to set strategy, the image shows it governed by an inflated domestic symbol, underscoring the tension behind cartel suspicions.
candidates.evidence: 10. ビール大手、染みついた国内志向 カルテル疑惑に透けるジレンマ（日経・読売・産経・47・みんかぶ）2026/10/09

evaluation.reason: A3 shows a scale inversion (a local bottle enlarged into the boardroom’s chair), which visually communicates that corporate decisions are dominated by local/domestic symbolism. The visual turn is clear, but the composition (many tiny executives, boardroom detail) is likely to lose clarity at 64 mm. Also it edges from metaphor into an implied factual claim that company governance is actually controlled by that local symbol/interest—a stronger assertion than the headline strictly provides.
unsupportedClaims: Depicts a modest local bottle as the actual seat of corporate authority — implying that company decision-making is literally governed by the local symbol or local interests (not established in the headline).
Shows executives seeking 'approval' from the bottle as if it issues directives, which asserts a causal control relationship beyond the article's text.

Executives in suits are tiny, clustered along the table, craning their necks and taking notes as they look up anxiously at the towering bottle. One executive stands on a step stool to reach the bottle's cap as if seeking its approval.
angleCandidates.reason: 大企業の意思決定が、実際には拡大された『地元』イメージに支配されているという本社と地域志向の矛盾をスケール変化で強調する。
angleCandidates.visualTurn: Scale shift: a modest local bottle is blown up to occupy the position of authority at the boardroom table, making the local-first instinct visually rule the big firm.
angleCandidates.contradiction: Although the firm is large and expected to set strategy, the image shows it governed by an inflated domestic symbol, underscoring the tension behind cartel suspicions.

angleEvaluations.reason: A1 makes a strong, immediately readable role-reversal: the public-facing executive waves the flag while strings show a humble shopkeeper actually pulling the levers. That directly inverts the expected protector/protected relationship and ties clearly to the 'domestic-first vs cartel' dilemma. However it asserts a specific actor (local shopkeeper) actually controlling the brewer—an unreported causal claim not supported by the supplied headline.
unsupportedClaims: Implies a local shopkeeper (a named or identifiable retailer) actually controls and directs the big brewer’s actions/strategy — not stated in the headline.
Implies a single local actor is the locus of cartel control/manipulation rather than depicting a general power imbalance or coordinated industry behaviour.

angleEvaluations.reason: A2 uses a simple, legible object inversion: cans repurposed as a physical barrier. That cleanly visualizes the paradox that ‘domestic preference’ can function as a blocker to competition, which maps closely to the headline’s suggestion of exclusion/cartel-like effects. It stays metaphorical rather than inventing a specific unreported actor or causal chain.

A3 shows a scale inversion (a local bottle enlarged into the boardroom’s chair), which visually communicates that corporate decisions are dominated by local/domestic symbolism. The visual turn is clear, but the composition (many tiny executives, boardroom detail) is likely to lose clarity at 64 mm. Also it edges from metaphor into an implied factual claim that company governance is actually controlled by that local symbol/interest—a stronger assertion than the headline strictly provides.
unsupportedClaims: Depicts a modest local bottle as the actual seat of corporate authority — implying that company decision-making is literally governed by the local symbol or local interests (not established in the headline).
Shows executives seeking 'approval' from the bottle as if it issues directives, which asserts a causal control relationship beyond the article's text.

paperArticleTitle: ビール大手、国内志向とカルテル疑惑
prompt:
Create a single editorial cartoon for English-speaking newspaper readers.
News headline (source evidence, not lettering): 10. ビール大手、染みついた国内志向 カルテル疑惑に透けるジレンマ（日経・読売・産経・47・みんかぶ）2026/10/09
Satirical angle: Render domestic-brand beer as a literal barrier that blocks market access, so the product itself becomes exclusionary architecture reflecting the cartel-suspicion dilemma.
Scene: In a supermarket aisle, oversized domestic beer cans are stacked into a continuous, high wall that separates customers on the near side from a shelf of foreign beers on the far side. A smiling brewery mascot on the near side adds another can to raise the barrier while shoppers press their hands against the wall trying to reach the blocked bottles.
Visual turn to show in the drawing: Object inversion: the product (beer cans), normally made for consumption, is repurposed as a physical blockade preventing access to competitors.
Depict this visible ironic reversal, not a literal reenactment of the reported event or a generic portrait. The turn must read without the title. A metaphor must not assert an unreported action or guilt.
Deliver the illustration alone. The page layout adds its title separately as real text. Do not render any title, subtitle, caption, heading or footer anywhere in this image, including the white margins. Do not write any Japanese characters in the image. Do not add text beneath the figures.
Strongly reference the pen-and-ink editorial cartoon work of Georges Bigot, Charles Wirgman and Charles Keene: observant human caricature, expressive faces and gestures, lively economical contours with deliberate changes in line weight, convincing clothing folds, and sparse hand-drawn hatching. Make these nineteenth-century draughtsmen the primary visual references throughout the drawing.
Create the original artwork for a newspaper illustration that will be printed using letterpress equipment and techniques from 150 years ago, circa 1876. Draw a deliberately composed, human-looking pen-and-ink original for an engraver to turn into a relief printing block. Use economical, clearly separated lines that remain legible when printed at small column size. Deliver the clean original drawing, without simulated aged-paper or printed-ink texture. Specific recognizable characters, expressive caricature, one clear visual joke, spare composition, natural asymmetry, varied purposeful contour lines. Avoid generic AI illustration conventions, glossy perfection, decorative clutter, stock robot imagery unless the joke specifically needs it, and irrelevant objects.
Black ink strokes on pure white paper ONLY. Clear outlines; express every shadow with sparse hatching, cross-hatching or stippled marks. Leave white paper visible between strokes. No gray fills, gradients, smooth shading, color, digital painting, photorealism, artificial paper texture or engraving filter effect. Keep most areas unshaded. Compact square composition, width:height exactly 1:1, complete subjects within the frame.
Design for a small newspaper column only about 64 mm wide. Use one clear visual joke with no more than two main figures and one essential prop. Remove secondary people, inset maps, small labels and ornamental detail. Render NO letters, numbers, symbols that resemble writing, speech bubbles, signs, stamps or pseudo-text anywhere in the image. Ignore ALL label or written-word instructions implicit in the headline, angle and scene except the one specified text element above. Never use fine print or tiny characters. Do NOT draw the Japanese title, a caption, a border, watermark or signature inside the image; the title will be typeset separately outside the artwork. Treat the scene as satire, and do not invent additional factual allegations beyond the supplied headline.
